evidence: app/package.json:5-17 — no tests means no noise, but also no signal
signal_to_noise.rationale: Per the rubric, no tests scores 3: no low-value tests to maintain, but nothing earning its keep either.

findings.issue: The app ships no test infrastructure whatsoever — no test script, no runner, no devDependencies — in a ~2000-LOC app whose logic is almost entirely data transformation and URL state.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (and optionally @solidjs/testing-library / Playwright for a couple of route-level smoke tests), a `test` script, and start with unit tests for lib/format.ts and the pure parts of lib/queries.ts.

findings.issue: refId parses IDs out of API URLs with a regex and returns 0 on mismatch; the id>10000 alternate-form guard (lines 292, 367, 416, 453) is duplicated inline four times. A refactor that changes either silently drops or admits species from every list.
findings.suggestion: Extract and unit-test the ID extraction and form-exclusion rules against fixtures with alternate forms (e.g. deoxys-normal 386 vs a Mega ID 10033).

findings.issue: fetchJson throws on any non-404 response but no ErrorBoundary exists (app/src/app.tsx:14 uses only Suspense); a transient API 500 leaves the page stuck on 'Loading…' and the not-found branch in app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:144-151 (which keys on data() === null, not undefined) never renders.
findings.suggestion: Add an ErrorBoundary in the router root with a retry message, and test the failure path with a stubbed 500.

findings.issue: The URL→input sync effect bails out while a debounce is pending (line 72), so navigating back during the 250 ms window (lines 50-64) discards the URL's q and re-navigates to the typed text — a race nothing pins down.
findings.suggestion: Cancel the pending debounce on popstate/URL change instead of ignoring the URL, and add a test that types then immediately presses Back.

findings.issue: Missing values must sort last in both directions (spec); sortRows hard-codes return 1/-1 for missing before applying direction. The natural refactor of multiplying the whole comparison by direction breaks this silently.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test sortRows directly with null power/accuracy rows in ascending and descending order.

findings.issue: Level-up moves deduplicate across version_group_details with Math.min on level; other methods keep the first detail seen. A subtle change here corrupts the Level column for Pokémon with per-version level differences.
findings.suggestion: Test the methodMoves construction with a fixture where the same move appears at levels 1 and 37 in the same version group.

findings.issue: Page clamping (parseInt || 1, min/max) and pageHref's hand-built query string are untested: out-of-range, zero, and garbage `page` values, and whether pagination links preserve an in-flight (undebounced) q, are all unpinned.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test currentPage/totalPages clamping and assert pageHref output for combined filter states.

findings.issue: Pure, instantly testable display helpers (humanize, latestEnglishFlavor's last-en-entry rule, collapseWhitespace, dexNumber zero-padding, formatMeasurement's em-dash for null) have no tests; regressions here violate the spec's display rules.
findings.suggestion: Five-minute vitest table tests over these functions; they encode the spec's exact formatting rules.

findings.issue: Type membership keeps the lowest slot per type then sorts by slot/name; slot-order bugs would mislabel dual-type Pokémon cards with no in-app guard.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the per-species type aggregation with a fixture containing duplicate type entries at different slots.

findings.issue: The #moves hash-scroll effect uses requestAnimationFrame and only runs client-side; untested, and its interaction with Suspense hydration is fragile.
findings.suggestion: Cover with a route test that loads /pokemon/pikachu#moves and asserts the moves section is scrolled into view.

summary: The app contains zero tests of its own — no runner, script, or dev dependencies — despite being dominated by pure data-transformation and URL-state logic that is cheap to unit-test. Everything currently passes only because the external acceptance suite in tests/ exercises the rendered pages end to end; once that suite is no longer the sole guard, refactors of refId/ID-exclusion, level dedup, missing-last sorting, and the debounce/URL sync would regress silently. Adding vitest coverage of lib/format.ts and the pure builders in lib/queries.ts, plus one error-boundary test, would be the highest-value first steps.
